HackerOne Security Research Report: Closing the Exposure Debt Gap

This title was summarized by AI from the post below.
HackerOne

372,585 followers

1w

Ten years ago, cybersecurity had a discovery problem. Today, it has a resolution problem. Security teams are remediating vulnerabilities 54% faster than two years ago but the open backlog of known, validated, unresolved findings has grown 131% in the same period. We call this gap Exposure Debt. On November 4, HackerOne is exploring the results of the 10th annual HackerOne Security Research Report in a live webinar to unpack what the data means for security leaders right now. We'll cover: → Why critical and high-severity findings are at a 5-year high → How 85% of researchers upskilling in AI is changing what gets found → Who takes the blame when AI gets it wrong (hint: 39% say the CISO) → Five actions the data supports to start closing the gap Register here: https://bit.ly/4s2P7Pv

    The start of a new year is often when security teams pause, look back, and recalibrate for what’s ahead. Over the last decade, vulnerability research has progressed through distinct phases—from coordinated disclosure to the first generation of bug bounty programs, and now to securing API-heavy, cloud-native applications. Each shift changed what researchers tested and how organizations responded. The 9th Hacker-Powered Security Report: Researcher Signals shows we’re entering another transition. As organizations integrate AI into their products at an unprecedented pace, security researchers are also incorporating AI into their workflows at a similarly rapid rate. This two-sided acceleration is reshaping how vulnerabilities are discovered and what high-impact findings look like today. The signals are already visible across nearly every dataset in the report. Read the latest insights as you set priorities for the months ahead 👉 https://bit.ly/4jo8u16 #Cybersecurity #SecurityResearch #HackerPoweredSecurity #SecurityLeadership

    Security teams are fixing issues faster than ever, but they’re still falling behind. Our 10th annual HackerOne Security Research Report reveals a growing disconnect between discovery and remediation: The average resolution time dropped from 135 days to 62 days. At the same time, the backlog of unresolved findings, or Exposure Debt, grew 131%. Teams are moving fast, but exposure is moving faster. That’s the problem with Exposure Debt. Fixing faster only works when remediation can keep pace with what you find. Dive into the full HackerOne Security Research Report: https://bit.ly/3TEbpum

    We put Anthropic’s Mythos 5 model up against our own code as part of Project Glasswing. The bigger story wasn’t just what it found. It was what happened next. Three things we learned: 1. Frontier models are making a real leap. Mythos found more vulnerabilities and more sophisticated ones. 2. Discovery is getting faster than remediation. A few weeks of scanning produced hundreds of findings. Finding vulnerabilities at this pace changes the challenge: teams need to validate, prioritize, and fix just as fast. 3. Better models demand better guardrails. As models become more capable, the work shifts from telling them how to reason to validating what they produce, ensuring complete coverage, and putting the right boundaries around how they operate. The takeaway: as AI accelerates vulnerability discovery, the security systems around it have to evolve just as quickly. Read the full write-up: https://bit.ly/4xQJIxn

    "Why pay a vendor when we can build this internally in a few weeks?" It’s a question most security leaders have asked themselves this year as AI dramatically accelerates how quickly code and products are built. But the reality isn't that simple: rip out the tooling you trust and rebuild from scratch, or keep paying for something AI might make obsolete? The reality is that while building a service might take a few weeks, maintaining it doesn't. Frontier models change every few weeks, and the constant tinkering required to keep pace can quietly swallow an entire security team.
